clue.text: Skilled but unpolished equestrian?

parts.note: reads as a horseman who is talented yet lacks polish, but describes one who breaks in untrained horses

explanation.surface: A capable horseman whose style is still crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a rider who is rough round the edges; in fact the phrase names someone who tames wild horses, or a US cavalry volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-breaker is a skilled horseman whose job is taming unbroken mounts, hence an unpolished but able equestrian.

clue.text: Work with aluminium and stone

parts.note: OP is the standard short form of opus, a work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A craftsman combines metal and rock in a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gemstone with a milky iridescent sheen.

clue.text: The doctor takes the complete round in a rush

indicators.note: the doctor takes the other pieces inside, holding them within his letters

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
the complete amount is all of it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A physician hurries through his whole ward round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast run, especially a horse's fastest pace, is a rush.

clue.text: Studying for university

explanation.surface: A student preparing for higher education.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying a subject is called reading it in British usage; the other sense is the University of Reading, in a Berkshire town west of London.

clue.text: Stamps and disappears

explanation.surface: Postage vanishes from the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal stamps for impressing coins or shapes are this; also the verb for fading away or ceasing to live.

clue.text: Repudiate touching homily

parts.note: re means about or concerning, touching on
a tract is a short moralising pamphlet, a sermon in print

explanation.surface: Disowning a moving sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back or withdraw a statement is to repudiate it.

clue.text: Shabby fellow who'd make a poor player the object of his gibes

parts.note: to rag someone is to make them the target of teasing jibes
taken as written
a muffin is old slang for a clumsy, inept player at a game

explanation.surface: A scruffy man mocks an incompetent sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'rag a muffin': to rag is to tease, and a muffin is an old word for a duffer at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin in ragged dirty clothes is a shabby fellow.

clue.text: The person taking charge of one's will

definitions.text: The person taking charge of one's will

parts.words: The person taking charge of one's will
parts.note: suggests an executor handling a testament, but means someone who controls another's mind through trance

explanation.surface: An executor managing someone's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' suggests a legal testament; it is the power of choice, taken over in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: One who induces trance states can control a subject's volition.

clue.text: In time of war youngsters have to be guarded

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the words war youngsters

explanation.surface: Children must be careful during wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautious and watchful, keeping up one's defences.

clue.text: Meal in part cooked as required by convention

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Etiquette demands some of the meal be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative assembly is a formal convention of representatives.

clue.text: Get back say into the shower

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: rain is a shower of water from the sky
say introduces an example, eg

explanation.surface: Recover by heading into the bathroom, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost is to get it back.

clue.text: Like the page being seen in jewellery, it's grating

indicators.note: the first pieces are seen within the jewellery, placed inside it

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
as means like, in the manner of
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A page boy wearing a ring makes an irritating noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh scraping voice or sound is grating.

clue.text: The way a speedy individual gets the bird in America

parts.note: a road is a way
a runner is someone who moves fast

explanation.surface: A fast traveller on the highway catches a bird in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast-running cuckoo of the American southwest deserts.

clue.text: Grant horse needs exercising, but not over a long distance

indicators.note: exercising means working the letters around into new shapes

explanation.surface: Grant's horse needs training, but not for long races.
explanation.definitionFit: Effective or operating only over small distances, as a missile or forecast.

clue.text: Interrogate cook

explanation.surface: Question the chef.
explanation.definitionFit: To question intensely, or to cook under direct radiant heat.

clue.text: Bill is of some consequence

explanation.surface: An invoice that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice or statement of charges; and in 'of account', meaning significant.

clue.text: A woman over fifty making the entry of the year

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An older woman gets into the record books for the year.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'over' places the woman above, ahead of, A and fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A record of the events of a single year is one entry in a chronicle.

clue.text: Note the weakest of the litter appears sound

parts.note: G is a musical note
the runt is the smallest, weakest animal in a litter

explanation.surface: The smallest piglet makes a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A low guttural noise, such as a pig makes.

clue.text: A refusal by a Frenchman (not named)

parts.note: taken as written
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A man from France turns something down, unidentified.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, so nameless or unattributed.

clue.text: Small creatures turning in the most fearless way

indicators.note: turning means the letters found are read backwards
the letters are found inside the run of most fearless

explanation.surface: Tiny beings twisting with great bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts, small amphibians, are known by this old word.

clue.text: Don't sink launch

explanation.surface: Keep afloat, set out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on the surface of water; also to start a company by offering shares.

clue.text: Competency of well-suited head

parts.note: fit means suitable
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A capable person with an appropriate leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitability or capability for a role is competency.

clue.text: One of many six-footers engaged in high-rise building

definitions.text: One of many six-footers engaged in high-rise building

parts.words: One of many six-footers engaged in high-rise building
parts.note: suggests tall construction workers on a tower, but means a six-legged insect building a tall mound

explanation.surface: A tall labourer working on a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall people; it means creatures with six feet, insects that build tall mounds.
explanation.definitionFit: These white-ant insects live in colonies and build towering earth mounds.

clue.text: Go on about a race coming to a beastly end

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rail is to complain at length, go on
taken as written
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Ranting about a race reaching its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of a rodent is the end of an animal; also a fish and a hairstyle.

clue.text: A pupil left nearer collapse

indicators.note: collapse means the word falls down into a new order

explanation.surface: A student left closer to breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is being taught is a pupil.

clue.text: Ordering beer at a discount

indicators.note: ordering means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting beer cheaply at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial refund or reduction in price.

clue.text: A quarter taken down can be put to rights

parts.note: N for north is a compass quarter
eaten means swallowed, taken down

explanation.surface: Something partly dismantled can be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy up, make orderly.

clue.text: Spirits — and they sound like it

indicators.note: sound like says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: it refers back to spirits, in the sense of gin, the drink

explanation.surface: Ghosts whose name is like a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to 'Spirits' in its alcoholic sense: gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Supernatural beings of Arabian lore are spirits.

clue.text: Listen to the man with car failing to start!

parts.note: he is the man

indicators.note: failing to start means the word car loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Pay attention to the man whose car won't start.
explanation.definitionFit: To give heed to, take notice of.

clue.text: Dropped new deal in time

indicators.note: new means the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh agreement dropped at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocked out of a competition, removed.

clue.text: So with a certain hesitation make a move

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
to go is to make a move

explanation.surface: Thus, hesitantly, take action.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used in logic.

clue.text: Viewers should hold on to catch "the poets"

indicators.note: the viewers should hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: seers are those who see, viewers
taken as written
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Viewers should keep watching to see the poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of fourteen-line verse are poets.
